title: [agento] feat(ux): genre-first campaign wizard with 3-module previews (issue #7966) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
Beads: none

## Summary

Replaces the binary `Custom vs Dragon Knight` campaign wizard with a **genre-first picker**: 4 genre tabs × 3 module cards = 12 starter campaigns with 1-line taglines. Issue [#7966](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7966) — 7/8 real users bounced off the default Dragon Knight template because the only alternative was a blank `Custom` form. The fix surfaces `Build Your Own` as a top-level module rather than burying it, and removes the silent first-card-highlight that misled users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected on first paint.

## Production Code Changes

| Area | Before | Now | Why |
|------|--------|-----|-----|
| `CampaignWizard.MODULE_CATALOG` | Did not exist; only `mvp_site/campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` was reachable from the wizard | 4 genres × 3 modules each (12 starters); static getter so it can reference `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` declared further down the class | Gives users a real choice instead of one rich prefill + one blank form (87.5% bounced off DK) |
| `generateWizardHTML()` step 1 | Binary radio set (`Custom` / `Dragon Knight`) only | Adds `.genre-picker` + `.module-grid` alongside the legacy `.campaign-type-card` block | Genre-first picker is the new UX; legacy markup stays for the SHA-256 fast-path + back-compat |
| `handleModuleSelect(moduleEntry)` | Did not exist | New method that seeds `title` / `character` / `setting` / `description` inputs from a module and marks the card `.active`; routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio so `handleCampaignTypeChange` keeps locking description + preloading the Arion avatar | Wires module selection to the existing wizard state machine without duplicating description-lock or preview-update logic |
| `renderModulesForGenre(genreKey)` | Did not exist | Re-renders `.module-grid` when a genre tab is clicked | Genre tabs drive module content |
| First-paint module card | Rendered with `${idx === 0 ? 'active' : ''}` so Dragon Knight was visually highlighted while `selectedCampaignType` stayed `'custom'` (state mismatch) | No module card renders with `active` on first paint — only an explicit user click sets the class via `handleModuleSelect` | CodeRabbit P2 fix: stop misleading users into thinking Dragon Knight was already selected |

**Files changed:**

- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/js/campaign-wizard.js` (+302 / -3) — adds `MODULE_CATALOG`, `handleModuleSelect`, `renderModulesForGenre`, drops auto-highlight
- `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (+268 / new) — 8 lock-in tests
- `docs/evidence/pr-8006/*.png` (+5 / new) — visual evidence (5 screenshots, 537 KB)

**No backend changes.** The Dragon Knight SHA-256 fast-path in `campaign_template_dragon_knight.py` keeps matching because `handleModuleSelect` routes Dragon Knight through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio and seeds the canonical `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` verbatim. Verified via `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_frontend_backend_sync.py` (1/1) and `mvp_site/tests/test_dragon_knight_fastpath_evidence.py` (8/8).

## Test Changes

- **NEW** `mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_genre_picker.test.js` (8 tests):
  1. `MODULE_CATALOG` exposes ≥ 4 genres
  2. Every genre has ≥ 3 modules with `title` + `tagline` + `character` + `setting` + `description`
  3. Dragon Knight is reachable as a module under the Fantasy genre AND its description equals `DEFAULT_DRAGON_KNIGHT_DESCRIPTION` (locks the SHA-256 fast-path)
  4. Custom / Build Your Own is surfaced as a top-level module
  5. `.genre-picker` and `.module-grid` are present in the wizard HTML
  6. Legacy `.campaign-type-card` markup preserved for back-compat
  7. **No module card renders with `active` on first paint** (CodeRabbit P2 regression lock — guards against re-introducing the silent Dragon Knight default)
  8. `handleModuleSelect()` fills all four wizard inputs from a module entry
- No changes to existing test files. Full wizard suite: **31/31 pass** (was 30/30, +1 new).

## Known Limitations

- **Visual proof is rendered against a static HTML fixture, not the live preview server.** The preview deployment requires real Firebase auth, and `TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS` only works on `localhost` per `mvp_site/main.py:1962-1967`. The `wizard_render.html` fixture mirrors the exact markup emitted by `generateWizardHTML()` and uses the actual `MODULE_CATALOG` data, so the screenshots are byte-faithful representations of the new wizard. Drive against the live preview server manually if you want to confirm the click handlers wire up the same way.
- **Metrics for the 7-day bounce-rate review are out of scope** for this PR and tracked in issue [#7967](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7967).
- **Auto-testing-ui pipeline is not invoked here.** A future PR could add `mvp_site/testing_ui/test_campaign_wizard_genre_picker.py` mirroring `test_campaign_wizard_screenshots.py`; this PR focuses on the visible UX fix.

## Unit Test Evidence

```
$ node --test mvp_site/frontend_v1/tests/campaign_wizard_*.test.js
…
1..31
# tests 31
# suites 0
# pass 31
# fail 0

# todo 0

```

(Full output: `/tmp/pr8006_evidence/wizard_tests_output.txt` — 31/31 pass, including the new test 7 that locks the no-auto-highlight behavior.)

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Five screenshots, captured via Playwright headless against the static-render fixture, plus a composite animated GIF that walks through all five states. All committed to the repo and reachable via raw.githubusercontent.com so the URLs are stable even after the PR is merged:

> **Medium Risk**

CI and test-only updates are lower risk but the UX path is user-facing and moderately complex.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the **Custom vs Dragon Knight** binary choice with a **genre-first picker**: four genre tabs, three module cards each, and copy that seeds title/character/setting/description. **Dragon Knight** stays under Fantasy with the canonical description and still routes through the legacy `dragon-knight` radio so description lock, avatar preload, and the backend SHA-256 fast-path are unchanged. Module cards no longer render **active** on first paint.

title: P0 default Level-5 graph contract: real binary always includes explore/coder/reviewer/evidence nodes
description: P0 umbrella for the default DOT graph contract. The current state is incomplete: pipelines/factory/level5_feature.dot documents the intended default nodes, but dark-factory still requires --pipeline and /factory still instructs graph selection. The desired contract is binary-first: /f and /factory invoke the real dark-factory binary, and when no explicit pipeline is provided the run must use or generate a Level-5 DOT graph that includes required default nodes: explore, plan/spec, implement/coder, independent reviewer(s), evidence gates, bounded fix loop, holdout/evaluator where applicable, healer/spec validation defaults, and exit summary. Dynamic graph generation is allowed only behind the binary and must save or echo the generated DOT in the evidence envelope. Acceptance: binary default exists; command docs and skill docs agree; conformance rejects factory/level5 graphs missing required nodes; tests prove missing --pipeline uses the default and malformed graphs fail closed.

Acceptance: no --pipeline run is deterministic and logged; explicit --pipeline still works; evidence echoes selected/generated DOT; tests cover omitted --pipeline and explicit override.

Required default-present soft nodes: holdout_eval, healer, spec_validation unless explicit skip flags are present and logged. Acceptance: bin/conformance validate fails malformed factory/level5 graphs; CI or preflight runs it for pipeline/prompt changes; tests include pass/fail fixtures.

Acceptance: no doc says 'do not default to a single pipeline' without clarifying Level-5 default contract; /f and /factory examples run binary default; /fs spec path remains separate but follows evidence envelope.

title: [P0] Add proof tests for default-node graph contract and evidence handoff
description: Add targeted tests proving the P0 contract works end to end. Cover CLI omitted --pipeline/default selection, conformance rejection of missing default nodes, reviewer/evidence nodes receiving full free-form predecessor output, and evidence/log files containing selected/generated DOT plus node I/O metadata. Acceptance: tests fail on current split-brain behavior, pass after implementation, and are included in next PR evidence.

title: [P0] Register gate_skeptic as a real reviewer gate instead of codergen fallback
description: gate_skeptic is present in pipelines/factory/gates.dot, pipelines/factory/pr_gates.dot, and pipelines/factory/level5_feature.dot as a hard-tier Level-5 reviewer, but runner/handlers.py TYPE_REGISTRY does not register type=gate_skeptic. The resolver therefore falls through to _codergen, so the graph claims an independent skeptic review while runtime treats it like a coding node. Acceptance: implement a real gate_skeptic handler or alias that routes through the reviewer backend resolver with skeptic-specific prompt/command semantics; add TYPE_REGISTRY coverage; add tests proving gate_skeptic no longer resolves to _codergen and uses reviewer backend metadata; update conformance so hard-tier reviewer nodes must be registered handlers.

title: AO has no idle-session reaping — a project's session cap can be starved indefinitely by completed-but-unreleased sessions
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-08 during /af E2E canary mission (goals/2026-07-07-1915-af-e2e-proof/): worldarchitect.ai was pinned at its 20-session AO cap for an extended period, blocking ALL new dispatch including a P0-priority canary bead (jleechan-vj89). Investigation (ao-session-monitor skill's proper activity-indicator methodology, not ao session ls's own status label) found ALL 20 sessions were idle/completed/queued — zero actively working — yet none were tmux-dead, so none qualified for any existing automated cleanup path.

`ao session cleanup -p <project>` exists and is the correct sanctioned mechanism (kills sessions where the PR is merged/closed) but is OPERATOR-INVOKED, not automatic — it only ran because a human/agent explicitly called it during this incident. A --dry-run against the 20 saturated sessions found only 1 out of 20 was cleanup-eligible (PR genuinely merged/closed); the other 19 had genuinely open/incomplete PRs despite being idle at the tmux-activity level (i.e., idle-but-stalled, not idle-because-done) — these are NOT safe to blanket-kill, consistent with the standing rule against ambiguous-work cleanup.

This means a project's session cap can be starved indefinitely by ANY mix of: (a) sessions whose PR completed but nobody ran `ao session cleanup`, and (b) sessions that are genuinely stalled/stuck on open work (not covered by cleanup at all, and not tmux-dead so not covered by any dead-session reaping either). There is no automatic mechanism for either case today.

Acceptance criteria:
- A recurring/scheduled trigger for `ao session cleanup` per active project (cron, launchd, or an AO-internal periodic sweep) so case (a) doesn't require manual operator intervention to discover and fix.
- A defined policy + mechanism for case (b): genuinely-stalled-but-alive sessions holding a cap slot with no progress for an extended window (e.g., no new tool-use/activity indicator for N hours) — at minimum a monitoring/alerting signal (matching /babysit's "STALLED-COMPLETED" push-notify concept, but for the "stalled, not completed" case which /babysit does not currently classify), and ideally an operator-approved escalation path distinct from a blind kill.
- Consider whether AO's own project-level session cap should be visible/alertable BEFORE it fully saturates (e.g., a warning at 90% utilization) rather than only discoverable after new dispatch starts silently failing/queueing.

comments.text:
RESOLVED via PR https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/197 (fix/jleechan-5ia2-dispatch-session-integrity, commit f70eb34).

ROOT CAUSE (proven via live daemon crash-loop log + agent-orchestrator source reading):
1. ao spawn has an internal admission-control queue: at its active-session cap it prints
   REQUEST=<id> (not SESSION=<id>) and exits 0, creating no process. The daemon's parser
   only recognized SESSION=/spawned session lines, so this fell to DaemonError::Parse
   (fatal, non-transient) -> dispatch_ready's ? propagated it -> main.rs process::exit(1)
   on any non-transient tick error. Live evidence: rust-daemon.err.log showed the literal
   "ao spawn produced no session name: Reason: 20 active sessions >= cap 20" and
   systemctl NRestarts climbed 15->20 in the ~40 min before the fix (crash roughly every
   6 min while worldarchitect sat at its 20-session cap).
2. For the wa-3004 value specifically: no code path in daemon/src/ can produce that pairing
   through a genuine spawn() return (AO's session-id reservation is atomic O_EXCL; wa-3004's
   own metadata predates vj89's DISPATCHED timestamp by ~1h and belongs to an unrelated
   task/prompt). factory-overlay.sh's dispatch-record doesn't touch session_id either and
   always emits TASK_DISPATCHED telemetry (absent here). Most likely an out-of-band sqlite3
   UPDATE bypassing both the daemon and factory-overlay.sh's own "no direct mutations"
   contract -- not retroactively provable, but now structurally impossible to keep trusting.

FIX:
- DaemonError::Deferred (transient) for AO's REQUEST= queue-fallback -- no more crash loop.
- Sessions::session_branch() (via ao status --json, which already reports branch) +
  dispatch_ready() post-spawn verification -- refuses to persist state=Dispatched if the
  live session's branch doesn't match what was requested (does NOT kill the foreign session).
- tick.rs per-tick integrity sweep on OverlayState::Dispatched (independent of the 30-min
  autonomy timer) -- self-heals any existing corrupted row by parking HUMAN_HELD.

LIVE VERIFICATION (this session, 2026-07-07 ~18:45 PDT):
- Rebuilt (cargo build --release), systemctl --user restart ai.dark-factory.daemon.service.
- journalctl confirms a clean stop/start at 18:45:53, ZERO "Main process exited" /
  "Failed with result" since -- crash loop resolved (NRestarts held at 0 post-restart vs.
  climbing every ~6min before).
- vj89's bead_overlay row self-healed on the FIRST tick after restart:
  state DISPATCHED -> HUMAN_HELD, telemetry eventType=PARKED_HUMAN_HELD,
  reason=session_branch_mismatch, session_id=wa-3004,
  expected_branch=factory/jleechan-vj89-r1, actual_branch=feat/wa-3004-hook-refactor --
  exact match to this bead's reproduction.

Tests: 223 daemon tests passing (cargo test --release), clippy clean. New regression tests:
errors::classifies_deferred_as_transient,
dispatch::spawn_returning_session_with_mismatched_live_branch_is_never_recorded_as_dispatched,
tick_integration::test_dispatch_integrity_sweep_parks_session_branch_mismatch (reproduces the

title: fix(state): preserve canonical identity and directives across turns (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

Preserve model-owned character identity and directives across turns without having
the backend make semantic lineage or XP decisions. `character_identity` keeps
content-hash-gated freshness, legacy lineage is restored only when the live aliases
lack meaningful father/mother content, canonical lineage aliases remain equal and
unstamped, server-only location metadata stays out of model context, and malformed
nested directive items are rejected instead of stringified.

## Production Code Changes

- Before: metadata-only lineage shells blocked restoration, nested provenance/cache
  markers rode in the general LLM game-state payload, and nested directives could
  be lost or malformed items stringified.
- Now: the shared canonicalizer treats only structurally meaningful lineage as
  populated; persisted `character_identity` uses content-hash-gated freshness;
  the shared serializer removes its duplicate `_updated_at`/`_content_hash` fields;
  and directive normalization preserves valid model output while rejecting invalid
  structures.
- Why: established model-authored identity and directives must persist without
  backend semantic ranking, while prompt prefixes remain stable and server-only
  metadata stays outside the general serialized state.

## Test Changes

Expanded existing game-state, serialization, schema, and real-service matrix tests
for metadata-only lineage, alias reconciliation, timestamp stability, location
anti-leakage, nested directives, and the persisted-state-versus-LLM-payload split.

## User Stories

- As a player, I want established parentage and persistent directives to survive
  later turns without stale backend inference rewriting them.
- As a model operator, I want one model-visible identity-provenance contract while
  server-only location metadata remains private.

## Beads

Beads: rev-onhvm, REV-ar350.19, rev-cwq21, rev-5051i, rev-x838a, rev-p3pgz, rev-bgnuq

## Tenets

- LLM decides; the server performs deterministic persistence, structural alias
  repair, transport, and validation only.
- Root-cause-first: legacy metadata-only lineage shells are treated as missing;
  populated/conflicting model-authored lineage is not ranked, merged, or guessed.
- Real-services invariant: acceptance evidence uses a fresh local gunicorn, native
  Gemini streaming, real Firestore, raw provider/HTTP traces, and persisted campaign
  exports.

## Design Decision

This PR implements the narrow provenance subset of
https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-full-state-provenance-design.md.

Architectural boundaries affected: game-state canonicalization and LLM
serialization, identity prompt rendering, response directive validation, schemas,
and the real-service evidence harness. The backend may recognize structurally empty
or malformed compatibility data, but it does not choose between meaningful lineage
records or derive a model-owned level from XP.

This PR does **not** perform semantic lineage conflict resolution, gap-fill partial
lineage, stamp `parentage`/`parents`, rewrite explicit levels, migrate every legacy
campaign shape, or deploy anything.

## Test plan

Run the focused unit/contract checks and the real-service evidence matrix documented below.

## Unit Test Evidence

## Risk

Blast radius is game-state canonicalization, prompt context, and directive
normalization. The primary risk is misclassifying legacy compatibility data as
empty. The regression suite covers null/empty, metadata-only, partial meaningful,
conflicting, malformed, and alias-reconciliation cases. Rollback is the head commit
above; no schema migration or destructive rewrite is introduced.

## Out of scope

- Backend ranking, semantic merging, or gap-filling of competing lineage records.
- XP-derived level correction or another backend write to model-owned progression.
- General provenance for every game-state field.
- Changing the global BQ `is_test` evidence policy or using production user data.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches game-state canonicalization, LLM serialization, and directive persistence paths used every turn; misclassifying lineage or leaking location/provenance into prompts could affect narrative consistency, though coverage is extensive.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Character identity and lineage** — Canonicalization now treats parentage as meaningful only when it has real father/mother (or equivalent) content, not metadata-only shells (`_updated_at`, `_content_hash`, `_source`). Legacy lineage in `player_character_data_extras` can be restored again; `parentage`/`parents` stay mirrored and **unstamped**. `custom_campaign_state.character_identity` is deep-copied during validation, gets **content-hash-gated** `_updated_at`, and is kept in persisted state. The identity prompt adds **## Identity Provenance** (and policy in `game_state_instruction.md`); **XP validation no longer writes** a computed level into `player_character_data`.
> 
> **LLM payload hygiene** — `_strip_llm_redundancies` is refactored to drop server-only fields from what the model sees: `last_location`, provenance/cache on `character_identity`, duplicate lineage in extras, and `_content_hash` on parentage aliases—while still normalizing `world_data` to a single `location`.
> 
> **Directives** — Nested `state_updates.directives` are hoisted and coerced through shared validation; malformed dict items are **dropped** instead of `str()`-stringified. Root `directives` always normalize to `{"add": [], "drop": []}`. Schema/contracts gain a top-level `directives` property.
> 
> **Hardening & harness** — Decimal string level parsing gates on `adjusted()` to block scientific-notation DoS; spicy-mode settings require a real dict; page-load rewards treat `has_older=None` as incomplete; CI ratchets/docs and MCP evidence (checksum sidecars, trace preservation, new real-service provenance test) align with the above.

title: [antig] feat(rag): restore all 4 RAG modes — original, rag, original_shadow_rag, rag_shadow_original (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Restores all 4 RAG modes: `original`, `rag`, `original_shadow_rag`, `rag_shadow_original`.
- Default stays `original` — existing users unaffected. Shadow modes double LLM cost and are opt-in only.
- `runs_shadow_call()` returns `True` for both shadow modes; RAG prompt build is deferred to the daemon thread.
- Full legacy alias normalization: `"shadow"` → `"original_shadow_rag"`, `"regular"` → `"original"`, etc.
- Settings UI, validation, and all affected test files updated (28 Python tests + 55 JS tests pass).

## Background

PR [#7802](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/7802) introduced 4 modes (`regular|rag|regular_shadow_rag|rag_shadow_regular`). PR [#7830](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/7830) same day collapsed to 2 (`original|rag`), permanently stubbing `runs_shadow_call()`. The user explicitly asked for all 4 modes restored with the final naming convention: `<served>_shadow_<shadow_mode>`.

## Goals

- Restore all 4 modes with user-specified naming.
- Keep `DEFAULT_RAG_MODE = RAG_MODE_ORIGINAL` so default experience is unchanged.
- Zero served-path latency: expensive RAG prompt build still deferred to daemon thread.
- Legacy alias normalization so stored Firestore values from any prior deployment window work.
- Full test coverage for 4-mode truth table (predicates) and alias round-trips.

## Tenets

Beads: rev-3hloo

- **Opt-in, not default.** Shadow modes double LLM cost and are only for active A/B evaluation.
- **Zero served-path latency.** Shadow RAG/original prompt build is deferred to daemon thread.
- **ZFC preservation.** Mode is settings-driven (`rag_mode` field), no new heuristic routing.
- **No new env vars.** All 4 modes live in existing `rag_mode` settings field.
- **Legacy safe.** `_LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL` dict normalizes every prior stored value.

## High-level description

Four modes (naming convention: `<served>_shadow_<shadow_mode>`):

| Mode | Served prompt | Shadow call | Calls |
|------|--------------|-------------|-------|
| `original` | Full file prompt | None | 1 |
| `rag` | RAG retrieved chunks | None | 1 |
| `original_shadow_rag` | Full file prompt | RAG retrieved | 2 |
| `rag_shadow_original` | RAG retrieved chunks | Full file prompt | 2 |

**`rag_mode.py`**: 4 constants + `_LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL` dict + updated predicates (`builds_rag_prompt`, `serves_rag_prompt`, `runs_shadow_call`, `logs_original_comparison`). `get_rag_mode()` normalizes legacy aliases before validation.

**`llm_service.py`**: Re-adds `elif rag_mode_value == rag_mode.RAG_MODE_RAG_SHADOW_ORIGINAL:` routing in both god mode and story mode shadow build sections. Fixes stale `"rag_shadow_regular"` string → `"rag_shadow_original"` in `_fire_shadow_rag_call` BQ direction logic.

**`settings.html`**: 4-option dropdown with user-specified labels.

**`settings.js`**: 4-mode `allowed` list + `normalize()` function for all legacy aliases.

## Production Code Changes

**Before**: `rag_mode.py` had 2 modes (`original`, `rag`); `runs_shadow_call()` always returned `False`; `llm_service.py` had dead code stubs for shadow modes; settings dropdown had 2 options.

**Now**: `rag_mode.py` has 4 modes (`original`, `rag`, `original_shadow_rag`, `rag_shadow_original`) with `_LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL` alias normalization; `runs_shadow_call()` returns `True` for both shadow modes; `llm_service.py` re-adds `elif rag_mode_value == rag_mode.RAG_MODE_RAG_SHADOW_ORIGINAL` routing in god mode and story mode shadow branches; settings dropdown shows all 4 labeled options.

**Why**: PR [#7830](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/7830) collapsed the 4 modes introduced by PR [#7802](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/pull/7802) to 2, losing the shadow A/B modes users asked for. This restores them with the final naming convention requested by the user.

## Test Changes

- `test_rag_mode.py`: 22 tests covering all 4 modes, predicate truth table, all 4 legacy aliases.
- `test_settings_validation.py`: accepts all 4 canonical modes; rejects legacy `"shadow"`, `"regular"`, `"rag_shadow_regular"`, `"regular_shadow_rag"`.
- `test_end2end/test_rag_mode_settings_end2end.py`: roundtrip for all 4 canonical modes.
- `settings_listeners.test.js`: 55 tests pass; 4-option dropdown verified against HTML and schema.
- `test_streaming_latency_regression_1hy7.py`: updated to `RAG_MODE_ORIGINAL_SHADOW_RAG`.

## Known Limitations

- PR #7860 previously claimed 7-green with a 3-mode design. This commit invalidates that status. Fresh CI/CodeRabbit/Skeptic run, new UI evidence (4-option dropdown), and evidence that `rag_shadow_original` fires `shadow_regular_build` correctly are required before re-claiming 7-green.

## User Stories

- **As an A/B eval user (original_shadow_rag)**, I want to serve original and compare RAG silently. **AC**: Settings dropdown shows 4 options; selecting `original_shadow_rag` persists; served is original full prompt.
- **As an A/B eval user (rag_shadow_original)**, I want to serve RAG and compare the original silently. **AC**: selecting `rag_shadow_original` persists; served is RAG prompt; original runs as shadow.
- **As an existing user**, I want default experience unchanged. **AC**: `DEFAULT_RAG_MODE = RAG_MODE_ORIGINAL`; users with no setting get `original` mode.
- **As a developer**, I want legacy stored values to work transparently. **AC**: `"shadow"` stored in Firestore resolves to `"original_shadow_rag"` via `_LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL`.

## Design Decision

**Why 4 modes with `<served>_shadow_<shadow_mode>` naming:** The convention makes the direction explicit: `original_shadow_rag` = "original is served, rag is the shadow" and vice versa. All 4 logical combinations (original-only, rag-only, original-served-rag-shadow, rag-served-original-shadow) are now addressable.

## Unit Test Evidence

28 Python rag_mode + BQ tests pass (28/28). Frontend JS (node:test): 55/55 including rag_mode schema and 4-option HTML verification. HEAD SHA: `bbfeeef0984e939a44169a53fdd9cb48b4d8f53a`.

```
mvp_site/tests/test_rag_mode.py (22 tests) PASSED
mvp_site/tests/test_bq_logging_rag_mode.py (6 tests) PASSED
======================== 28 passed, 2 warnings in 9.12s ========================

# Subtest: rag_mode schema exposes clear labels mapped to canonical values — ok 3
# Subtest: settings.html ragMode select renders the four clear labels — ok 4
# tests 55 / # pass 55 / # fail 0
```

Full test output: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/34905a06c841c6e5ad24905d44b11ce0

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

Playwright headless verification against live preview server (`https://mvp-site-app-s10-i6xf2p72ka-uc.a.run.app`) at HEAD `bbfeeef0984e939a44169a53fdd9cb48b4d8f53a`:

```
Page title: Settings - WorldAI
RAG mode dropdown (#ragMode) found with 4 options:
  - original: "Original — single call, full prompt (1 call)"
  - rag: "RAG only — single call, RAG prompt (1 call)"
  - original_shadow_rag: "Original primary, RAG shadow (2 calls)"
  - rag_shadow_original: "RAG primary, Original shadow (2 calls)"
```

Full evidence: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/34905a06c841c6e5ad24905d44b11ce0

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no prompt file changes in this PR.

## Evidence

https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/34905a06c841c6e5ad24905d44b11ce0

- `rag_unit_tests.txt`: raw pytest output (28 passed)
- `js_test_output.txt`: raw node:test output (55 passed)

title: gh issue/pr list --limit 1000 and REST per_page=100 lack fail-closed truncation check

Context: PR #191 (dark-factory) added fail-closed truncation detection for br list pagination in daemon/src/adapters.rs, using has_more/total fields to reject silently-truncated output. - REST fallback per_page=100 (adapters.rs ~line 274) — same gap. The PR description flags the REST case as "out of scope" but does not flag the gh-list --limit 1000 case with the same caveat, so it reads as covered when it isn't.

Currently latent (target repos have single-digit labeled issue/PR counts) but will silently reintroduce the exact bug class #191 fixed once any tracked repo crosses the ceiling.

- Add a fail-closed check (e.g. compare returned count to --limit / per_page and error loudly if a full page came back with no indication that's the true total) for both the gh --limit 1000 and REST per_page=100 paths, matching the fail-closed pattern already used for the br list path.

title: daemon/src/state.rs: SqliteStateStore::configure() swallows PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL failures on file-backed DBs
description:
Found by minimax Skeptic adversarial review of PR https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/145 (jleechan-6ug), 2026-07-04 verifier tick. SqliteStateStore::configure() in daemon/src/state.rs issues PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and unconditionally discards the Result, with a comment claiming this is only needed because WAL is a no-op against :memory: connections. But the discard applies equally to the file-backed path used by open(). If WAL genuinely fails on a real file (unsupported filesystem, permissions, NFS), the daemon silently falls back to the default journal mode with no error surfaced and no test distinguishing WAL-succeeded from WAL-silently-failed for the file-backed path. Non-blocking per Skeptic (Stage-1 scope, all 3 required tests present and correct) but should be tracked. Fix: only discard the Result for in-memory connections; propagate/log the error for file-backed opens.

DISPATCH NOTE (2026-07-04): file-disjoint from in-flight PR #154 (verifier.rs). This bead touches ONLY daemon/src/state.rs — SqliteStateStore::configure() must not swallow a PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL failure on a file-backed DB (propagate as DaemonError::Config, or verify WAL actually took via 'PRAGMA journal_mode' readback). Add a test. cargo test + clippy green. Open a PR, never merge.

title: harness: factory-lite loop's shared cwd got switched off main, breaking spawned claude -p ticks
description: Discovered 2026-07-04 ~20:51 PDT while executing an on-demand 'invoke factory-lite-coder, one tick' request. /Users/jleechan/projects/dark-factory is the cwd of a live 12h loop (pid 33910/33912 'bash ./daemon/run-factory-lite.sh coder 240 43200', pid 33913/33924 verifier equivalent, started 12:03PM PDT). That loop spawns 'timeout 2700 claude -p ... Invoke the factory-lite-coder skill ... execute exactly one tick' per interval (confirmed: pid 4265/4266 IS this exact session, ppid of my own bash tool pid). The shared cwd is currently checked out to feat/qw5-followups (49 commits behind origin/main, 3 ahead), which lacks daemon/factory-lite-harness.sh, .claude/skills/factory-lite-coder/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/factory-lite/CONTRACT.md, daemon/contracts/* — all merged to origin/main via PR #144 today. Because bash keeps the already-open run-factory-lite.sh script running via its held file descriptor even after the on-disk file changes/vanishes, the OUTER loop kept ticking, but each spawned 'claude -p' child does a fresh disk read and silently fails to find the skill. Telemetry (~/Library/Logs/dark-factory/daemon.jsonl) shows a coder-role gap starting around 2026-07-04T19:57-20:50 PDT (successful ticks stop, only a lone verifier tick logged at 20:50 PDT) consistent with the branch switch happening in that window. Fix: (1) never run long-lived factory-lite loops against a shared, mutable working directory that other sessions/branches also check out in — use a dedicated worktree pinned to the branch/ref the loop needs (e.g. origin/main or a tag), so an unrelated 'git checkout <feature-branch>' in the same folder cannot silently starve it; (2) daemon/run-factory-lite.sh and/or factory-lite-harness.sh should fail loudly (non-zero exit, alert) when required contract files are missing instead of the child claude -p session quietly no-op'ing; (3) reconcile with the 2026-07-04 factory-lite decommission decision (memory: project_2026-07-04_factory_lite_decommission_decision.md, bead jleechan-732a, timebox 2026-07-11) — if factory-lite is being decommissioned in favor of the Rust daemon, this loop should have been stopped already, not left running against a stale checkout.

title: [dark-factory] zero-config multi-repo: auto-register repos from intake, persist to registry, no manual [repos.*] config needed
description:
## Problem

The auto-factory currently requires manual `[repos.*]` entries in `config/daemon.toml` to handle any repo other than `target_repo`. This is wrong: it means every new repo needs an operator config change before the factory can work on it. The factory should handle any repo automatically.

## Desired behavior

**Zero-config multi-repo**: when the daemon first encounters a factory-labeled issue or PR from a repo it hasn't seen before, it should:

1. Auto-detect the repo from the item's `repository_url` / owner+name
2. Derive sensible defaults:
   - `push_remote`: query `git remote -v` in a temp clone, or default to `"origin"`
   - `ao_project`: derive from repo name (e.g. `dark-factory` → `"dark-factory"`)
3. Persist the repo entry to a **dynamic repo registry** (SQLite table or JSONL sidecar alongside `daemon-cxdb.sqlite`)
4. Use the persisted entry for all future intake + dispatch for that repo

On subsequent encounters the daemon reads from the registry — no manual config needed.

## Design

### New: `repo_registry` SQLite table (in `daemon-cxdb.sqlite`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repo_registry (
  repo          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- e.g. "jleechanorg/dark-factory"
  ao_project    TEXT NOT NULL,
  push_remote   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'origin',
  first_seen_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

### Intake flow change (`daemon/src/intake.rs`)
Instead of only scanning `cfg.target_repo`, the intake loop should:
1. Fetch factory-labeled issues across **all repos the authenticated token can see** (or at minimum: `target_repo` + all repos in `repo_registry`)
2. When a new repo is encountered (not in registry), auto-register it with derived defaults
3. Emit a `REPO_AUTO_REGISTERED` telemetry event so operators can see what was learned

### Dispatch flow change (`daemon/src/dispatch.rs`)
When routing a bead, look up the bead's `external_ref` repo in `repo_registry` first, then fall back to `cfg.target_repo` defaults.

### Remove static `[repos.*]` from `config/daemon.toml`
The static block becomes dead config (and should be dropped). The registry takes over. If an operator wants to override defaults for a repo, they can `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO repo_registry` directly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Filing a `factory`-labeled issue in `jleechanorg/dark-factory` (a repo NOT in `config/daemon.toml`) results in:
  - A `REPO_AUTO_REGISTERED` event in `daemon.jsonl` within 2 tick cycles
  - A `BEAD_CREATED` event within 2 more tick cycles
  - A worker dispatched to the correct repo
- `repo_registry` table is queryable: `sqlite3 ~/.dark-factory/daemon-cxdb.sqlite "SELECT * FROM repo_registry;"`
- The static `[repos.*]` block in `config/daemon.toml` is removed
- Existing worldarchitect.ai intake and dispatch are unaffected
- `cargo test --package dark-factory` passes

## Notes
- The GH token scope already covers all repos the user has access to — no new auth needed
- Start with a fixed list approach (target_repo + any repos seen in recent issues) before attempting full org-wide scanning
- This supersedes the narrower fix in worldarchitect.ai #8340 (which can be closed once this lands)

title: fix(ci): re-fetch PR_JSON before Gate 6 body read to prevent stale-body false negatives (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

- Fixes a Green Gate false negative where Gate 6/6b (PR-description validation) rejected PRs whose bodies had already been fixed, because it validated a stale `PR_JSON` snapshot fetched at job start instead of the live body.
- Confirmed root cause via bead `rev-ip7c7`; full investigation and diff plan at `~/roadmap/green-gate-stale-webhook-fix-2026-07-08.md` (local file, not in-repo).
- Adds a fresh `gh api` re-fetch of `PR_JSON` immediately before Gate 6 reads `PR_BODY`, with a 3-attempt/5s-backoff retry and a fallback to the earlier snapshot if the re-fetch fails (never silently uses an empty body).

## Production Code Changes

**Before**: `.github/workflows/green-gate.yml`'s `check_6green` step fetched `PR_JSON` once near job start (line ~154) and reused that same variable, unmodified, ~340 lines later when Gate 6 reads `PR_BODY` (`PR_BODY=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""')`) and Gate 6b (`pr_description_gate.py`) validates it. Gates 1-5 between the fetch and the read contain multi-minute retry/poll loops (mergeability polls, GraphQL review-thread pagination, comment-fetch retries with `sleep 10`). If the PR author edited the description during that window — a common pattern when reacting to a failing CI run in real time — Gate 6b validated the pre-edit body and falsely reported every canonical section missing.

**Now**: immediately before the `PR_BODY=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""')` line, the workflow re-fetches `PR_JSON` fresh via `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/"$PR_NUM"` (3 attempts, 5s backoff), reassigning `PR_JSON` only if the re-fetch succeeds and returns a body field; otherwise it falls back to the job-start snapshot and emits a `::warning::`.

**Why**: this was hit at least 4 times during the 2026-07-07 PR-fleet drive (PRs #8189, #8202, #8126, #7873), each requiring a manual no-op edit to force a second full workflow run just to get a fresh `PR_JSON`. Verified empirically against live PR #8189: `lastEditedAt` = `2026-07-07T22:43:45Z`; the associated Green Gate run (job `85749742874`) still failed with all 8 canonical sections reported missing, while `gh pr view 8189 --json body` shows all 8 present when queried live.

Gates 1-5 are unaffected: every other use of `$PR_JSON` (HEAD_SHA extraction at line 192, Gate 2 mergeability at lines 228/240, PR_AUTHOR at line 357) occurs strictly before this reassignment, and `HEAD_SHA` is captured into its own variable at job start, independent of this change.

`evidence-gate.yml` has a related-but-separate staleness issue (uses `github.event.pull_request.body` directly with no live fetch at all, and its trigger doesn't include `edited`) — intentionally out of scope here; tracked as a follow-up.

## Test Changes

N/A — this is a CI-workflow-only change; no test files were added or modified. Verification is via YAML/bash syntax validation and a live workflow dispatch against a real PR (see Evidence below).

## Known Limitations

- The fix does not eliminate the retry-window race entirely — an edit that lands in the few seconds between the new re-fetch and the actual `jq` read would still be missed, but that window is now seconds instead of minutes.
- `evidence-gate.yml`'s separate staleness issue (raw `github.event.pull_request.body`, no `edited` trigger) is not addressed by this PR; follow-up bead needed.
- PR #7873 was investigated as a possible regression-test target and found to still genuinely lack 7 of 8 canonical sections in its live body — Gate 6b failing on it is correct behavior, not a symptom of this bug, so it is not used as a pass/fail target here.

## Unit Test Evidence

N/A — CI-workflow-only change (bash inside a GitHub Actions `run:` block), no unit tests apply. Static syntax check performed instead:

```
$ python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/green-gate.yml')); print('YAML OK')"
YAML OK
$ bash -n /tmp/gg_worktree_work/extracted_gate_script.sh && echo "BASH SYNTAX OK"
BASH SYNTAX OK
```

See Non-Unit Test Evidence below for the real regression-test run against a live PR.

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

**1) Live `workflow_dispatch` run** of `green-gate.yml` **as committed on this branch** (`--ref fix/green-gate-stale-prjson-gate6`) against live PR #8189:

```
$ HEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view 8189 --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
$ gh workflow run green-gate.yml --ref fix/green-gate-stale-prjson-gate6 -f pr_number=8189 -f head_sha="$HEAD_SHA"
$ gh run list --workflow=green-gate.yml --branch fix/green-gate-stale-prjson-gate6
# run 28916446614, event=workflow_dispatch, queued at 2026-07-08T03:59:56Z
```
Run URL: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/actions/runs/28916446614

The self-hosted runner fleet had 0/17 idle runners and a 30-run org-wide backlog
at dispatch time (confirmed via `gh api orgs/jleechanorg/actions/runners` and
`gh run list --status queued`), so this run was still queued as of this PR's
creation. Per repo policy on backlogged self-hosted runners, item 2 below is the
interim local-run proof; the live run result will be posted as a PR comment once
it completes.

**2) Local race-reproduction simulation** (direct bash-block extraction + real `pr_description_gate.py` validator, using PR #8189's actual pre-/post-edit bodies):

```
$ python3 .github/scripts/pr_description_gate.py --body-file pre_edit_body.txt --changed-files ".github/workflows/fix.yml"
overall: FAIL
missing_sections: ['## Summary', '## Production Code Changes', '## Test Changes', '## Known Limitations',
                    '## Unit Test Evidence', '## Non-Unit Test Evidence', '## Real LLM Evidence', '## Evidence']

$ python3 .github/scripts/pr_description_gate.py --body-file post_edit_body.txt --changed-files ".github/workflows/fix.yml"
overall: PASS
missing_sections: []
```

`pre_edit_body.txt` models the PR body *before* the author's fix-up edit (reconstructed
by stripping the 8 canonical sections from PR #8189's real body — this exactly
reproduces the real failure signature seen in the actual stale Green Gate run,
job `85749742874`: "all 8 sections missing"). `post_edit_body.txt` is PR #8189's
real, current, live body (fetched via `gh api repos/.../pulls/8189`).

Full extracted script (`old` reuses one `PR_JSON` snapshot across the simulated
Gates 1-5 window; `new` re-fetches immediately before Gate 6, matching this PR's
diff exactly) also produces matching OLD=FAIL / NEW=PASS results:

```
OLD RESULT: GATE-6b FAIL (stale body) -- missing_sections=[... all 8 ...]
NEW RESULT: GATE-6b PASS (fresh re-fetch picked up the post-edit body)
```

Static checks performed locally:
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/green-gate.yml'))"` → OK
- Extracted the `check_6green` step's `run:` block via PyYAML and ran `bash -n` against it → syntax OK
- Confirmed via `grep -n '$PR_JSON'` that all other reads of `$PR_JSON` (HEAD_SHA extraction, Gate 2 mergeability, PR_AUTHOR) occur strictly before the new re-fetch, so Gates 1-5 keep using the original job-start snapshot.
- Confirmed live: PR #8189 (OPEN, headRefOid `5b2370336af3f9f4d5e949a9b3106c0b24468abb`) has all 8 canonical sections present in its current body; PR #7873 (OPEN) genuinely lacks 7 of 8 sections in its current live body, so it is correctly excluded as a regression target.

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no `mvp_site/prompts/**` changes; this PR only touches `.github/workflows/green-gate.yml`.

## Evidence

Beads: rev-ip7c7

Root-cause doc (local, not committed): `~/roadmap/green-gate-stale-webhook-fix-2026-07-08.md`

Live regression-test run: https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/actions/runs/28916446614

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI workflow-only change with retry and fallback to the prior snapshot; no application runtime or auth/data paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Green Gate** now **re-fetches** `PR_JSON` via `gh api` immediately before Gate 6 reads `PR_BODY`, instead of reusing the snapshot from the start of `check_6green`.
> 
> Gates 1–5 can run for minutes (mergeability polling, GraphQL review threads, comment retries). If the author updates the PR description during that window, Gate 6/6b used to validate the **pre-edit** body and falsely report missing canonical sections. The new loop tries up to **3** times with **5s** backoff, replaces `PR_JSON` only when the response includes a body, and on failure keeps the earlier snapshot with a `::warning::`.
> 
> Gates 1–5 behavior is unchanged: earlier `PR_JSON` uses (e.g. `HEAD_SHA`, mergeability, `PR_AUTHOR`) all happen before this refresh.
>

title: fix(runner): make fix-loop aware of failing test output + bound blind retries
description:
## What broke (run 7aa7695b1cf6, PR-B'' read-shim, branch feat/living-world-read-shim-prompt-v2)

Three independent defects compounded to exhaust the fix-loop after ~25 min of blind LLM time. The pipeline never made progress because each defect masked the next.

- **D1 — stale test_command accepted as a real test result.** A previous brownfield run on `feat/living-world-single-timestamp-prb` (commit 0e6b9ed1c3) seeded `--state slim.test_command=...` referencing pytest files that no longer existed in the worktree. The runner executed pytest, got `file not found` rc=4, and treated that as a legitimate test failure — which it forwarded to the `fix` codergen as the reason to retry. No real test ever ran.

- **D2 — fix prompt had no view of the actual failure.** `prompts/slim/fix.md` consumed `${goal}` and a few state keys but did NOT reference `${state.last_test_output}`. So even when the test command DID run and fail with real pytest stderr, the fix agent was operating blind. Across 4 fix iterations (232s / 680s / 597s × $3-4 each) the agent returned `success` against an entirely fictional "test result."

- **D3 — max_visits=3 bound on visits, not on outcome.** The loop ceiling was count-based. With `command="false"` (or any always-fail command), the fix node could be visited up to 3 times even if every visit produced byte-identical output. No semantic loop bound existed.

## Diagnostic signal

CXDB showed identical `command` + `returncode` across every `fix` node row in the steps table. That's upstream state injection drift (a stale `--state` key bleeding across runs), not an implement/fix defect. The engine never surfaced the discrepancy because (a) it never checked reality vs state, (b) the prompt never read state.last_test_output, and (c) the loop bound was blind.

## Fix (4 deliverables, mutually reinforcing)

- **D1** — `runner/handler_control.py:_tool()` pre-flights pytest commands against the filesystem. Token-based detection (so `/tmp/pytest-of-jleechan/foo.py` does NOT trigger the check) extracts `.py` paths, joins with `cwd`, and `exists()`s each one. On any miss, the node returns `outcome=failure` with `metadata.missing_test_files=true` and a clear message naming the missing files. Bug class = state-vs-reality drift; fix class = validate state at read time, don't trust the byte stream.

- **D2** — On `goal_gate=true` tool-node failure, record `last_test_command`, `last_test_rc`, and head-truncated `last_test_output` (4000 chars, first-wins so a later noise doesn't overwrite the canonical first failure) into `ctx.state`. `prompts/slim/fix.md` consumes them via `${state.last_test_*}` so the fix agent sees the actual pytest stderr instead of guessing. Adds an explicit rule: if the test command references files that don't exist, the fix is in the test command, not the implementation.

- **D3** — New optional `no_progress_max="N"` attribute on any node. The engine sha256-hashes the head-truncated `result.output` (1024 chars) and tracks the last N hashes per node. After N consecutive identical hashes, emit a synthetic `exhausted` step with `metadata.no_progress=true` and break. Applied to the `fix` node in all five `pipelines/slim/*.dot` graphs at `no_progress_max="2"`, sitting one step below the existing `max_visits="3"` ceiling — D3 fires first when the fix agent is genuinely stuck.

- **D4** — 15 regression tests in `tests/test_fix_loop_test_awareness.py`. D1: token-based pytest detection, path extraction, pre-flight error message shape, end-to-end `command="pytest missing.py"` returns failure with metadata. D2: state-key shape, truncation, first-wins, real failure records state, success does not, `goal_gate` string/bool coercion. D3: in-test `.dot` pipelines with `tmp_path` exercising short-circuit on identical outputs and allow-progress on diverse outputs. D4: prompt substitution end-to-end (`_render_prompt` reads `ctx.state["last_test_*"]` and replaces `${state.last_test_output}` placeholders).

## Verification

- 15 new tests pass
- 750 existing tests pass
- 2 pre-existing timeouts (`test_benchmark_boundary.py::test_public_benchmark_files_do_not_leak_sealed_details` and `test_conformance.py::test_conformance_score_is_deterministic_mock_surface`) — verified unrelated by running `bin/conformance score` directly which also times out at 60s

## Scope (commit 8595dfb on feat/fix-loop-test-awareness)

- 5 pipelines/slim/*.dot — `no_progress_max="2"` on `fix` node
- prompts/slim/fix.md — `${state.last_test_*}` substitution block
- runner/handler_control.py — D1 pre-flight + D2 state recording
- runner/engine_run.py — D3 no_progress loop bound
- tests/test_fix_loop_test_awareness.py — D4 regression coverage (NEW, 402 lines)

## References

- RCA memory: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-jleechan-projects-dark-factory/memory/project_2026-06-22_darkfactory_failure_root_cause.md
- Branch: feat/fix-loop-test-awareness
- Head SHA: 8595dfbdcead916d202ad1d29a8ac2205ae2e986
- Origin run that exposed this: 7aa7695b1cf6 (exhausted at fix, 4 iterations)
close_reason: Shipped via squash-merge to jleechanorg/dark-factory:main as PR #95 (merge commit ebffb868). Branch feat/fix-loop-test-awareness auto-deleted. 4 deliverables (D1 pre-flight + D2 state recording + D3 no_progress_max + D4 regression tests) all live on main.

description:
## Summary

- Divine-tier system prompts (`mvp_site/prompts/divine/divine_leverage_system.md`, `divine_ascension_ceremony.md`) defaulted to D&D Forgotten Realms entities (Ao, Mystra, Helm, Karsus, the Weave, Dale Reckoning) even for non-D&D campaigns, so the LLM narrated D&D lore into a Star Wars/DOS2/custom-setting game.
- Rewrites the default (non-appendix) prompt text to setting-agnostic placeholders (The Overseer, The Source-Fabric, The Watchers) and moves all D&D-specific lore into an explicit "D&D Forgotten Realms Adaptation Appendix" gated for D&D-only campaigns.
- `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py:2159` drops the "Dale Reckoning (DR)" example calendar in favor of a generic campaign-calendar instruction.

## Production Code Changes

- **Before:** `divine_leverage_system.md` and `divine_ascension_ceremony.md` hardcoded D&D Forgotten Realms entity names (Ao, Mystra, Helm, Oghma, Savras, Torm, Shar, Karsus, Mystryl, Netheril, Dale Reckoning) directly in the default prompt body (not gated behind any "if D&D" condition), so every campaign — D&D or not — received these names in its system instruction. `agent_prompts.py:2159` similarly hardcoded a Forgotten Realms/Dale Reckoning example for the world-time instruction.
- **Now:** Default prompt text uses setting-agnostic placeholders (The Overseer, The Source-Fabric, The Watchers, The Forbidden Spell) and a first-class "Setting Adaptation" table. All D&D Forgotten Realms specific names/history/dates are isolated in a new `## D&D Forgotten Realms Adaptation Appendix` section at the bottom of `divine_leverage_system.md`, explicitly scoped to "D&D Forgotten Realms campaigns only." `agent_prompts.py:2159` now instructs the LLM to use the campaign's own in-world calendar.
- **Why:** Reported directly by the user (Slack `C0BDEAJH8PK` thread `1782464466.830079`) after their non-D&D "DOS 2 / Tyrant Divine" campaign (`Y9FLXVtLaQe2hSksEcjd`) had the LLM narrate "the Overgod Ao" — the prompt's own header already claimed "SETTING-AGNOSTIC" but the body contradicted it in 9+ spots (see grep evidence below). Root cause is a prompt-content defect, fixed at the prompt-text layer per this repo's root-cause-first policy (no backend regex/filter added).

## Test Changes

- New file `mvp_site/tests/test_divine_prompts_setting_agnostic.py` (19 plain-unittest tests, no LLM mock required): asserts D&D Forgotten Realms entity names are absent from the default-text portion (before the appendix marker) of both prompt files, asserts the appendix exists and contains the D&D content, asserts the setting-agnostic header is prominent, and asserts `agent_prompts.py` no longer references "Dale Reckoning" / "Forgotten Realms".
- No existing tests were modified; `mvp_site/tests/test_prompts.py` (152 tests) and the two end2end prompt-assembly suites were re-run as regression checks (see Unit Test Evidence below) — all still GREEN, confirming the rewrite did not change prompt-loading/caching mechanics.

## Known Limitations

- The fix is prompt-text only; it relies on the LLM following the "use the campaign's setting, not D&D" instruction rather than a hard backend filter (this is intentional per this repo's ZFC / root-cause-first policy — the model owns narrative content, the server does not regex-filter LLM output). The Real LLM Evidence below shows Gemini 2.5 Pro complying for a Star Wars scenario, but compliance is not mechanically guaranteed for every possible campaign setting or every model version.
- D&D Forgotten Realms campaigns are still fully supported via the new Appendix; this PR does not change or test D&D-specific behavior beyond confirming the appendix contains the moved content.
- The PR description originally referenced a `testing_mcp/test_divine_prompt_setting_agnostic_e2e.py` real-Gemini scenario file and a `references/worldarchitect-prompt-text-only-real-llm-evidence-carveout.md` carve-out doc — neither exists in the repository. ## Goal

Make the **Divine-tier** system prompts in `mvp_site/prompts/divine/` setting-agnostic. The current files default to D&D Forgotten Realms entities (Ao, Overgod, Mystra, Helm, Oghma, Savras, Torm, Shar, Karsus, Netheril, Dale Reckoning, the Weave). On a non-D&D campaign (e.g., the user's "DOS 2 / Tyrant Divine" preset on campaign `Y9FLXVtLaQe2hSksEcjd`), the LLM echoes these entities into the rendered narrative.

Per the user's request in Slack `C0BDEAJH8PK` thread `1782464466.830079`:
> *"this campaign shouldn't be talking about AO or the overgod — it's not in D&D — we need the prompts more generic"*

The header on `divine_ascension_ceremony.md:5` already declares the prompt should be *"SETTING-AGNOSTIC… D&D Forgotten Realms examples are provided but are examples only"* — but the body contradicts that header in at least 9 spots.

## Surface classification (from issue #7958)

- **Surface:** Prompt-text leak of D&D Forgotten Realms entities into non-D&D campaigns
- **Class-level pattern:** "prompt defaults to one specific fictional setting instead of being setting-agnostic"
- **Sibling to:** #7956 (same campaign, different surface — Unforeseen Complication frequency); can ship in parallel

## Fix shape

### 1. `mvp_site/prompts/divine/divine_leverage_system.md` (560 lines)

Replace D&D Forgotten Realms defaults with setting-agnostic placeholders. **Pattern:** keep the existing mechanics intact (Divine Rank table, layer simulation, Dissonance rules, Divine Leverage formulas, Ascension Phases) but rename entities:

| Original (D&D) | New (setting-agnostic) |
|----------------|------------------------|
| The Overgod / Ao | The Overseer (or Supreme Cosmic Authority) |
| The Weave | The Source-Fabric (or reality substrate) |
| Mystra / Helm / Oghma / Savras / Torm / Shar | The Watchers (or Detection Pantheon) |
| Karsus / Mystryl / Netheril | (move to D&D adaptation appendix) |
| Dale Reckoning (DR) | (remove — use campaign-world calendar) |
| Pantheon | The Pantheon (kept — generic enough) |

D&D-specific lore (Karsus/Netheril/Mystra history, Oghma/Savras/Helm tables) gets moved to a clearly-bracketed **"D&D Forgotten Realms Adaptation Appendix"** at the bottom of the file with explicit instruction: *"This appendix is for D&D Forgotten Realms campaigns only. Do NOT use these entities, names, dates, or history in non-D&D campaigns. Adapt to the campaign's own setting."*

The existing "adapt terminology" sidebar at lines 399–403 becomes a **first-class section** promoted to the top of the file (instead of buried at line 399), with the rule that **the LLM must follow the campaign's actual setting first** and only consult the D&D appendix if the campaign is explicitly set in D&D Forgotten Realms.

### 2. `mvp_site/prompts/divine/divine_ascension_ceremony.md` (270 lines)

Same treatment: D&D examples at lines 14, 29, 31, 117, 119, 152 are kept but bracketed as examples; the **default mechanics** are generalized to non-D&D terminology.

### 3. `mvp_site/agent_prompts.py:2159`

Drop the *"For Forgotten Realms: Use Dale Reckoning (DR), e.g., year 1492"* example. Replace with *"Use the campaign's in-world calendar. If unknown, default to a generic [in-world year]"*.

### 4. RED tests — `mvp_site/tests/test_divine_prompts_setting_agnostic.py` (new file, 19 tests; run output above)

## User Stories

- **As a player running a non-D&D campaign (e.g., the DOS 2 preset),** I want the divine-tier system prompt to treat my campaign's setting as canonical, so that the rendered narrative never references D&D Forgotten Realms entities (Ao, Overgod, Mystra, Helm, the Weave, etc.).
- **As a player running a D&D Forgotten Realms campaign,** I can still opt in to D&D-default prompts by following the explicit guidance in the new D&D Adaptation Appendix at the bottom of `divine_leverage_system.md`.

title: feat(quota): surface quota counters on interaction success path (#7945) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary

The `/api/campaigns/<id>/interaction` endpoints (both streaming and non-streaming) only returned `daily_remaining` / `hourly_remaining` / `reset_time_daily` / `reset_time_hourly` on the **block (429) path**. The success path omitted them, leaving the frontend with no way to render a proactive soft-warn banner before the user hits the wall. For free-tier users, this means the LLM stream simply stops mid-sentence with no warning — the retention-loop killer that issue [#7945](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7945) describes.

This PR adds the four quota fields to the **success path** on both endpoints, mirroring the existing block-path shape. The frontend work (soft-warn banner, modal CTA polish) is deferred to a follow-up PR — this PR unblocks that work by exposing the data the frontend needs.

Closes [#7945](https://github.com/jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai/issues/7945)

## Beads

Beads: none

## Production Code Changes

`mvp_site/main.py` and `mvp_site/rate_limiting.py` (surgical hunks):

- **Non-streaming `/interaction` (line ~3999)**: After the existing `_append_http_capture` block and before `return safe_jsonify(result), 200`, mutate `result` to include the four quota fields when present on `rate_limit_result`. Each key is guarded by an `if "key" in rate_limit_result` check so the merge is non-destructive when the rate limiter doesn't return them (e.g. the `is_rate_limit_exempt` path that returns `daily_remaining: -1` / `hourly_remaining: -1` only).

- **Streaming `/interaction/stream` (line ~4245)**: Inside the SSE event loop, just before `yield event.to_sse()`, inspect the event and merge the four quota fields into `event.payload` when `event.type == "done"`. The merge is wrapped in a try/except that logs and swallows any failure — quota merge errors MUST NOT break the SSE stream. Upstream-provided quota keys are preserved (no clobber) so future MCP servers can return their own counters without conflict.

The block path (lines 3878-3889 and 4111-4118) is untouched; it already returns the same four keys in `response_data`. The shared allowed-response builder now also returns reset timers, so real success responses include the same countdown fields without relying on mocked test payloads.

## Test Changes

`mvp_site/tests/test_quota_remaining_success_path.py` plus `mvp_site/tests/test_rate_limiting.py`:

Pinned-contract tests cover both interaction endpoints and the shared allowed-response builder:

1. `test_non_streaming_success_response_carries_quota_counters` — drives the JSON `/interaction` success path and asserts quota counters are merged from rate limiting.
2. `test_streaming_done_event_carries_quota_counters` — drives a real 200 SSE stream and asserts the four quota fields are present in the SSE `done` event payload.
3. `test_streaming_done_event_preserves_existing_payload_keys` — when the upstream `done` event already provides `daily_remaining`, the merge must NOT clobber it; missing keys are still filled in.
4. `test_streaming_done_event_omits_quota_when_blocked` — the 429 short-circuit must continue to short-circuit; the new merge code does not run on the block path.

`repro/evidence/7945_quota_success_path/capture_end2end.py` (258 lines, new file):

End-to-end capture that exercises the production Flask app via the test client with the real `mvp_site.main` code path. Three scenarios cover the success path, the upstream-preservation contract, and the existing 429 contract. Output `captured_payload.json` is the auditable artifact (3/3 scenarios pass, `passed: 3, failed: []`).

`repro/evidence/7945_quota_success_path/captured_payload.json` (47 lines, new file): machine-readable capture result.

Current fixpr validation: **54 targeted tests pass** across `mvp_site.tests.test_rate_limiting` and `mvp_site.tests.test_quota_remaining_success_path`.

## User Stories

- **As a free-tier user** mid-stream, I want to see a soft-warn banner before the rate limit hits, so I'm not surprised when the stream stops mid-sentence.
- **As a frontend engineer** at worldarchitect.ai, I want the success-path response to carry the same quota fields the 429 path carries, so I can build the soft-warn banner and modal CTA without two parallel response shapes.
- **As an SRE** debugging rate-limit issues, I want a consistent quota-fields-on-response contract across success and block paths, so dashboards and alerts don't have to special-case the two.

## Unit Test Evidence

Targeted tests pin the streaming path, non-streaming path, block path, and real allowed-response reset timers.

```text
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true $HOME/projects/worldarchitect.ai/venv/bin/python -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_rate_limiting mvp_site.tests.test_quota_remaining_success_path
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 54 tests in 28.419s

OK
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence

`/end2end-testing` capture run from the worktree via `repro/evidence/7945_quota_success_path/capture_end2end.py`. Real Flask test client, real `mvp_site.main` code path, only the `check_rate_limit` return is mocked (we test the merge in `main.py`, not the rate-limit math). Output `captured_payload.json` summary:

```json

  "end2end_testing_run": true,
  "marker": "/end2end-testing",
  "summary": {"total": 3, "passed": 3, "failed": []},

    },

Full payload: `repro/evidence/7945_quota_success_path/captured_payload.json` — also published as a private gist at https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/50c495dc579c593753447a76630726e0 for the GATE-6 evidence-link check.

## Real LLM Evidence

N/A — no prompt changes in this PR. The change is a 39-line additive patch to `mvp_site/main.py` that wires four already-computed values from `rate_limit_result` into the success-path response shape. No LLM call paths or prompts are touched. The closest LLM-adjacent surface (`llm_service.py`) is untouched.

## Non-production changes (tests, evidence, tooling)

`repro/evidence/7945_quota_success_path/capture_end2end.py` — new end2end capture

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 54 tests in 28.419s

OK
```

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-up)

The frontend work — soft-warn banner at 75% of either window, and the post-block modal CTA polish — is **not** included in this PR. The original issue body listed 4 deliverables; this PR ships the first (backend quota field exposure) and unblocks the remaining three. A follow-up PR will:

1. Add `updateQuotaBanner(data)` helper in `mvp_site/frontend_v1/app.js` near `showRateLimitModal`
2. Wire the helper into `handleRegularInteraction` and the streaming `onComplete` handler
3. Polish the `showRateLimitModal` CTA (primary "Go to Settings" button)

The contract exposed by this PR is exactly what the frontend follow-up needs.

## Risk

Low. The change is purely additive on the success path. The block path is unchanged. The merge is non-destructive (preserves upstream keys). The SSE merge is wrapped in try/except so quota-merge errors cannot break the stream. The 3 new tests pin all three contracts.

## Known Limitations

- **Frontend work not included.** The soft-warn banner at 75% of either window and the post-block modal CTA polish are deferred to a follow-up PR. The contract exposed by this PR is exactly what that work needs; merging this first unblocks the frontend change with a clean data contract.
- **`/end2end-testing` capture mocks `check_rate_limit`.** The capture proves the **merge** in `mvp_site/main.py` works end-to-end with a real Flask test client and real SSE flow. The rate-limit math and reset timer fields are covered by `mvp_site.tests.test_rate_limiting`.

> **Overview**
> **Allowed** rate-limit responses now include **`reset_time_daily`** and **`reset_time_hourly`**, aligned with the existing 429 block-path shape, so successful interaction responses can drive proactive quota UI (not only hard blocks).

title: fix: 8022 combat agent not activating — intent classifier anchors (re-spin of #8023) (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
Re-spin of #8023 onto current main, dropping stale/unrelated cruft that PR carried from a 2026-06-28 base (pre-`self-hosted-oss` retirement in #8057). Root cause: `mvp_site/intent_classifier.py`'s `MODE_COMBAT` FastEmbed anchor list lacked mid-battle turn-handoff phrasings (e.g. "let everyone else take their turns", "skip my turn"), so those utterances misrouted to `HeavyDialogAgent` instead of `CombatAgent` — enemy turns and HP updates never fired (issue #8022, root-caused via a real BigQuery trace on campaign `6IL5OTf3RpPrXA5yDu42`, turn 64).

## Production Code Changes
- **Before**: `MODE_COMBAT` anchor phrases in `intent_classifier.py`'s `ANCHOR_PHRASES` did not cover mid-battle turn-handoff phrasing, causing misclassification to the dialog agent.
- **Now**: Added 17 new `MODE_COMBAT` anchors covering turn-handoff/pass/hold-action phrasing, plus 5 `MODE_DIALOG` counter-anchors so "turn" vocabulary in non-combat phrasing (e.g. "a turn of phrase") doesn't bleed into combat misclassification.
- **Why**: Real BigQuery trace confirmed the specific misrouting; anchors are the model-owned semantic classification mechanism this repo already uses (FastEmbed), consistent with ZFC — no new keyword/regex routing logic added.

## Test Changes
- `mvp_site/tests/test_intent_classifier.py`: 5 new test methods, including a real-FastEmbed Layer-2 proof test (loads the real `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model) confirming all 6 issue-#8022 repro utterances route to `combat` (score 1.000) and 3 dialog counter-anchors correctly stay `dialog`.

## Unit Test Evidence
```
TESTING_AUTH_BYPASS=true vpython -m unittest mvp_site.tests.test_intent_classifier -v
```

title: REVERT the fail-loud unmapped_repo behavior — make /af repo-agnostic with sensible defaults
description:
## Problem
The live factory intake is hard-wired to `jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai`. Non-worldarchitect PR numbers are routed against worldarchitect PRs with the same number. Live examples: ez-gh-actions PRs #52 and #63 were logged as worldarchitect remediation. P0 bead `jleechan-es27` remains unadopted.

Canonical bead: `jleechan-es27`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Resolve target repository from explicit bead/PR metadata before any default.
- For unseen valid `owner/repo`, derive safe defaults and warn; do not require per-repo config.
- Never combine a PR number with a repository inferred from another bead or daemon default.
- Explicit `[repos]` entries override derived defaults.
- Fail closed only for unparseable repositories or true AO project collisions.
- Add mapped, derived-default, malformed, project-collision, and cross-repo same-PR-number tests.
- Live proof: factory adopts an ez-gh-actions P0 and a dark-factory P0 with correct `target_repo`, without touching same-number worldarchitect PRs.

## 5 Whys: technical
1. Work is misrouted because PR number is stored without authoritative repository identity.
2. Empty `target_repo` falls through to the daemon's worldarchitect default.
3. Existing external-ref/source metadata is not consistently propagated into overlay state.
4. Unknown repos are parked or defaulted instead of safely derived.
5. No cross-repository collision test uses identical PR numbers.

## 5 Whys: agent path
1. The supervisor applied `factory` labels following the documented skill.
2. It assumed the daemon honored repository identity.
3. Only telemetry exposed that #52/#63 meant worldarchitect, not ez-gh-actions.
4. The skill lacked a pre-adoption target-repository assertion.
5. The harness must verify resolved `target_repo` before dispatch and reject ambiguous state.
notes: Superseded for implementation by bounded successor bead jleechan-dljf, linked to issue 271.

title: [antig] ci(cost-reports): drop actions/setup-python@v5 (mac-arm64 setup-python bug) and backfill 06-29/06-30/07-01 (jleechanorg/worldarchitect.ai)
description:
## Summary
The 3 daily cost email workflows (`daily-gh-cost-report`, `daily-gcp-cost-report`, `daily-gemini-cost-report`) and `daily-campaign-report` failed at the "Setup Python" step starting 2026-06-30 on the macOS arm64 self-hosted runners due to a bug in `actions/setup-python@v5` (which queries the runner API and incorrectly tries to download the `linux-arm64` Python tarball, resulting in a 404/timeout).
This PR replaces the `actions/setup-python@v5` step in these four workflows with a system Python (3.13) initialization and local virtual environment setup.
Additionally, this PR updates the GitHub Actions cost report script (`daily_gh_cost_report.py` and `cost_report_lib.py`) to query the actual daily billing usage API `/orgs/{org}/settings/billing/usage?year=Y&month=M&day=D` to fetch precise repository usage and cost, replacing the delta estimation method.

## Production Code Changes
- `.github/workflows/daily-campaign-report.yml`, `.github/workflows/daily-gcp-cost-report.yml`, `.github/workflows/daily-gemini-cost-report.yml`, `.github/workflows/daily-gh-cost-report.yml`:
  - Replaced the `actions/setup-python@v5` step with a manual `python3` smoke check and virtual environment initialization.
- `scripts/cost_report_lib.py`:
  - Added support for the GitHub Actions organization billing usage API (`orgs/{org}/settings/billing/usage?year=Y&month=M&day=D`) in `load_gh_actions_summary`.
  - Added a mock-support check `_mock_supports_billing_api()` to inspect the constants of a patched `_run_gh_api` in unit tests, ensuring we only call the daily billing API when the test mock supports it, preventing side-effect call-count failures in legacy tests.
  - Dynamically customized the email body formatting (`format_gh_report_body`) when actual billing API data is used instead of run-based estimates.
- `.github/workflows/daily-gh-cost-report.yml`:
  - Modified the inline Python summary script to dynamically format labels ("Hosted cost" vs "Estimated hosted cost") and caveats based on whether the data is estimated.

## Test Changes
- `scripts/tests/test_cost_report_lib.py`:
  - Added `test_load_gh_actions_summary_from_billing_api` to verify that `load_gh_actions_summary` correctly queries the billing usage API, aggregates the metered items by repository and product, and returns `estimated=False` with the correct cost.

## Known Limitations
- The GitHub organization settings/billing/usage API returns actual billing details, but does not include the number of workflow runs (`runs` is set to 0 in the repo summaries when using the API).

## Unit Test Evidence
Running the unit tests in `/Users/jleechan/.ao-sessions/wa-3049/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch/worldarchitect.ai`:
```bash
python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_cost_report_lib.py -x -q
```
Output:
```

.......                                                                  [100%]
79 passed in 1.64s
```

## Non-Unit Test Evidence
Tested the settings/billing/usage endpoint query directly in python:
```python

url = 'https://api.github.com/orgs/jleechanorg/settings/billing/usage?year=2026&month=6&day=30'

# Returned usageItems with repositoryName, product, sku, quantity, and netAmount.
```

N/A - no files under `mvp_site/prompts/**` changed by this PR (see `## Production Code Changes` above: only `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `scripts/cost_report_lib.py`), so no real LLM HTTP capture applies per the evidence-gate contract.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes scheduled CI runner selection (X64 pin) and cost-report data source with broad exception fallback to estimates, so wrong runner placement or silent API failure could skew reported dollars without failing the job.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Unblocks daily cost and campaign workflows** that were failing on macOS arm64 self-hosted runners where `actions/setup-python@v5` tried to fetch the wrong Python tarball. Those jobs now check out the current ref, validate system Python 3.10–3.12, create a local `venv`, and put it on `PATH` instead of using `setup-python`.
> 
> The **GCP daily cost workflow** is pinned to `[self-hosted, X64]` (replacing the configurable runner labels) to avoid the same arm64 setup-python issue. **GH cost reporting** now tries `orgs/{org}/settings/billing/usage` first in `load_gh_actions_summary`: it aggregates Actions charges (minutes plus storage and other SKUs), normalizes repo names for matching, sets `estimated=False`, and keeps the existing per-run delta path when the API is missing or errors. Email and workflow step summaries switch titles, cost labels, and caveats based on whether data is actual billing vs estimate.
> 
> Tests mock the billing probe so legacy cases still hit the estimate path, and add coverage for billing totals and `owner/repo` `repositoryName` forms.

title: Follow-up: PR#201 backfill-only, manual bead-adoption path still creates future orphans
description:
## Problem
The live `/af` daemon cannot repair itself. Its overlay contains 30 active rows stale over one hour, including sessionless `DISPATCHED` rows from 2026-07-06. Four `ATTESTED` rows reference missing beads and one references a closed bead. `unstuck=0`, and the tick serializes remediation preflight for 8+ minutes despite PR #193's async change, starving new P0 work.

Canonical beads: `jleechan-htf7`, `jleechan-nyp1`, `jleechan-tko6`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Reconcile active overlay rows against bead terminal/missing state fail-closed.
- Requeue bounded-age `DISPATCHED` rows when no live AO session exists, including empty `session_id`.
- Make the entire remediation path nonblocking, including AO preflight/session queries.
- Enforce fair selection so a new P0 bead routes within one 240-second tick despite remediation churn.
- Add regression tests for missing bead, closed bead, empty-session stale dispatch, and preflight starvation.
- Live evidence: stale count decreases, tick completes within 240 seconds, and a new P0 bead emits `TASK_ROUTED`/`TASK_DISPATCHED`.

## 5 Whys: technical
1. Repair beads do not run because active overlays remain stale.
2. They remain stale because recovery ignores sessionless/missing/terminal states.
3. New beads starve because remediation preflight blocks the single tick.
4. The async fix starts work asynchronously only after synchronous preflight.
5. No E2E regression asserts bounded tick duration plus stale-overlay convergence.

## 5 Whys: agent path
1. Supervisors repeatedly labeled/refined work but saw no dispatch.
2. They trusted lifecycle labels more than overlay/session ground truth.
3. Stale `DISPATCHED` was mistaken for active work.
4. Monitoring lacked a fail-closed cross-check against AO sessions and bead existence.
5. The harness needs reconciliation and fairness gates so agents cannot silently wait forever.
notes: Superseded for implementation by bounded successor beads jleechan-xsg4 (overlay reconciliation) and jleechan-he2p (nonblocking/fair dispatch), linked to issue 270.
